FastPath sends data traffic straight to the VMs, bypassing the ExpressRoute gateway, which removes the gateway as a throughput and latency bottleneck; it needs an Ultra Performance, ErGw3AZ or ErGwScale gateway (ErGwScale with at least 10 scale units). For resilience, use two circuits at two different peering locations to survive the loss of a location, or add a coexisting site-to-site VPN as a cheaper backup, making sure it does not advertise more specific routes so ExpressRoute stays preferred.

concepts.heading: Hub-Spoke Networks and Private DNS
concepts.body: In a hub-spoke design, the hub virtual network holds shared services such as Azure Firewall, VPN and ExpressRoute gateways, Azure Bastion and DNS, and each workload spoke peers with the hub. Peering is nontransitive: two spokes can each reach the hub but not each other through it. To send spoke-to-spoke traffic through central inspection, place the firewall in the hub and add user-defined routes in every spoke that point to the firewall's private IP. Spokes use the hub's gateways through gateway transit on the hub side and use remote gateways on the spoke side, so on-premises routes reach every spoke. Private DNS zones resolve private endpoints inside Azure, but on-premises DNS servers cannot query them directly; an Azure DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint in the hub, targeted by on-premises conditional forwarders, gives on-premises clients the private addresses. An outbound endpoint forwards Azure queries to on-premises DNS.

concepts.heading: Azure Virtual WAN
concepts.body: Azure Virtual WAN is a Microsoft-managed networking service built around virtual hubs. A Standard virtual WAN connects all hubs in a full mesh and gives any-to-any transitive connectivity between branches over site-to-site VPN, users over point-to-site VPN, ExpressRoute sites and attached virtual networks, all over the Microsoft backbone. Hubs can be secured with Azure Firewall, managed through Firewall Manager, to inspect traffic centrally. The Basic type supports only site-to-site VPN, so most designs need Standard. Choose Virtual WAN when a scenario lists many branches, remote users, ExpressRoute in several regions and a need for transitive routing with little routing work, because Microsoft runs the hub routers and gateways. Prefer a customer-managed hub-spoke network when you need network virtual appliances or custom routing that Virtual WAN does not support, or when only a few spokes and one connection are involved.

examPoints: A question about a fixed outbound IP range for an allowlist, SNAT port exhaustion or no inbound exposure is testing NAT Gateway on the subnet.

A question that names a gateway bottleneck, office-to-office traffic, regions on other continents or a lost peering location is testing FastPath, Global Reach, the Premium add-on or two circuits at two locations.
A question with many branches and users needing managed transitive connectivity, or spokes that cannot reach each other, is testing Virtual WAN Standard versus hub-spoke with firewall routes.

quiz.q: A Flexible scale set scales between 2 and 40 VMs and calls a partner API that allows only a small, fixed range of source IP addresses. The VMs must not accept inbound internet connections, and SNAT port exhaustion has caused failures. What should you recommend?
choices: A Standard public IP on every VM, so each instance has its own fixed outbound address
Outbound rules on the existing Standard Load Balancer, with its frontend IP given to the partner
A NAT gateway with a public IP prefix attached to the subnet that the scale set uses
A route that sends the subnet's internet traffic to a VPN gateway that connects to the partner
quiz.explain: NAT Gateway gives the whole subnet outbound addresses from one prefix, allocates SNAT ports dynamically and allows no inbound connections. Choice B is tempting because outbound rules also give a fixed IP, but they pre-allocate a limited number of ports per instance, which is what runs out, and keep an inbound frontend.

quiz.q: A company connects its datacenter to Azure through one ExpressRoute circuit at a single peering location. Risk management requires private connectivity to continue if that whole peering location goes offline. What should you recommend?
choices: Enable the Premium add-on on the circuit so it can use peering locations on other continents
Enable FastPath on a gateway SKU that supports it so traffic bypasses the virtual network gateway
Add a second connection from the same circuit to a zone-redundant ExpressRoute gateway
Add a second circuit at a different peering location and connect both circuits to the gateway
quiz.explain: Only a second circuit that terminates at another peering location survives the loss of the first location. Choice A is tempting because it mentions other locations, but Premium extends which Azure regions the circuit reaches; the circuit itself still ends at one peering location.

days.recap: Use Standard public IPs and NAT Gateway for outbound, zone-redundant active-active VPN gateways, ExpressRoute with Premium for other geopolitical regions, Global Reach between sites, FastPath past the gateway and two locations for resilience, hub-spoke with firewall routes and DNS Private Resolver, and Virtual WAN Standard for many branches.

days.title: Network Security and Load Balancing: Firewall, NSGs, Private Link, DDoS, WAF, and Traffic Routing

concepts.heading: Azure Firewall SKUs
concepts.body: Azure Firewall is a managed, stateful network firewall that usually sits in the hub and inspects traffic between spokes, to and from on-premises, and to the internet. Basic fits small environments: FQDN filtering for HTTP, HTTPS and SQL traffic, and threat intelligence in alert mode only. Standard adds network-level FQDN filtering, web categories, a DNS proxy and threat intelligence that can alert and deny. Premium adds outbound TLS inspection as a forward proxy, a fully managed IDPS with signature-based detection, and URL filtering on the full path, including for decrypted HTTPS traffic. So a requirement to block malware inside encrypted downloads or filter by URL path points to Premium. Azure Firewall policies, managed through Firewall Manager, can be shared across hubs and regions. For inbound web traffic, terminate TLS and apply a WAF with Application Gateway or Front Door; Microsoft's comparison lists inbound TLS termination for Azure Firewall as done through Application Gateway.

concepts.heading: NSGs and Application Security Groups
concepts.body: A network security group holds stateful allow and deny rules on source, destination, port and protocol, applied to a subnet or a network interface, and it is the basic segmentation control inside a virtual network. Service tags, such as Storage, Sql or AzureFrontDoor.Backend, stand for Microsoft-maintained address ranges so rules do not track IP lists. Application security groups let you group network interfaces by role, such as web, app and db, and use those groups as the source and destination of NSG rules. A rule such as allow web to app on port 8443 keeps working as VMs are added or replaced, because new NICs simply join the group; no IP addresses are edited. Use NSGs and ASGs for east-west segmentation inside and between subnets, and Azure Firewall for central, FQDN-aware and threat-aware filtering across the network. Both are often combined in one design.

concepts.heading: Private Endpoints Versus Service Endpoints
concepts.body: Both keep traffic to Azure PaaS services on the Microsoft backbone, but they work differently. A service endpoint extends a subnet's identity to a service such as Storage or SQL; the resource keeps its public endpoint, and its firewall allows that subnet. It costs nothing extra and needs no DNS change, but on-premises clients cannot use it. A private endpoint gives a specific resource a private IP address in your virtual network through Private Link. It is reachable from peered networks and from on-premises over VPN or ExpressRoute, the resource's public network access can be disabled, and because it maps to one resource it helps prevent data exfiltration to other accounts. It needs DNS: a privatelink private DNS zone linked to the virtual networks, and a DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint for on-premises resolution. Private Link service lets you publish your own service behind a Standard Load Balancer to consumers' private endpoints.

concepts.heading: DDoS Protection and Web Application Firewall
concepts.body: Every Azure public IP gets basic infrastructure DDoS protection. DDoS IP Protection is enabled per public IP and suits a few protected IPs. DDoS Network Protection is a plan associated with virtual networks that protects the public IPs of resources in them, across subscriptions in the tenant, and adds DDoS Rapid Response support, cost protection for scale-out during a documented attack and a WAF discount. Many public IPs, or a need for rapid response and cost protection, point to Network Protection. A web application firewall blocks Layer 7 attacks such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting. Run it on Front Door for global apps, at the edge, or on Application Gateway WAF v2 for regional apps. On Front Door, the Standard tier supports custom WAF rules, while Premium adds the Microsoft-managed rule set, bot protection and Private Link to origins whose public access is disabled. DDoS protection and WAF complement each other.

concepts.heading: Choosing a Load Balancing Service
concepts.body: Learn's decision tree asks two questions: is the app global or regional, and is the traffic HTTP(S)? Azure Front Door is the global Layer 7 entry point: clients connect to the nearest edge location, it caches content, applies WAF and fails over quickly between origins in several regions. Traffic Manager is DNS-based, works for any protocol and routes with priority, weighted, performance, geographic, multivalue or subnet methods; failover waits for DNS caches to expire, and geographic routing pins users to a region for compliance. Azure Load Balancer is a regional Layer 4 service for TCP and UDP, zone redundant on the Standard SKU; its global tier gives a static anycast IP in front of regional load balancers, preserves the client IP and fails over without DNS. Application Gateway is the regional Layer 7 load balancer with URL path routing, TLS termination, autoscale and WAF v2. Designs often combine them, such as Front Door in front of Application Gateway in each region.

examPoints: A question that asks for TLS inspection, IDPS or URL path filtering on outbound traffic is testing Azure Firewall Premium, and one about rules that survive VM churn is testing application security groups.
A question about private IP access from on-premises with public access disabled is testing private endpoints with private DNS and DNS Private Resolver, not service endpoints.

A question that combines global or regional reach with HTTP or non-HTTP traffic, WAF, a static anycast IP or geographic compliance is testing Front Door, Application Gateway, global Load Balancer and Traffic Manager.

quiz.q: An Azure SQL Database logical server must be reachable from virtual networks and from on-premises over ExpressRoute private peering, with public network access disabled. On-premises clients must resolve the server's usual name. What should you recommend?
choices: A Microsoft.Sql service endpoint on each subnet, plus a server firewall rule for the on-premises range
A private endpoint for the server, its privatelink DNS zone and a DNS Private Resolver inbound endpoint
A NAT gateway on the hub subnet, with the server's firewall allowing only the NAT gateway's IP prefix
Server firewall rules that allow the ExpressRoute Microsoft peering prefixes, with public access on
quiz.explain: A private endpoint gives the server a private IP reachable over private peering, public access can be disabled, and the resolver lets on-premises forwarders resolve the privatelink zone. Choice A is tempting because service endpoints also secure access, but they keep the public endpoint and do not work from on-premises.

quiz.q: A public web app runs in one Azure region. Requests under /api must go to one VM pool and requests under /images to another, TLS must end at the entry point, and a WAF must block SQL injection. Which service should you recommend?
choices: Azure Application Gateway WAF v2 with path-based routing rules to the two back-end pools
Azure Traffic Manager with performance routing and one endpoint for each of the two paths
A Standard Load Balancer with two load-balancing rules, one for each of the two URL paths
A global Azure Load Balancer with one regional load balancer in its back end for each path
quiz.explain: Application Gateway is the regional Layer 7 service that routes by URL path, terminates TLS and runs WAF v2. Choice C is tempting because a Standard Load Balancer is regional and zone redundant, but it works at Layer 4 and cannot read URL paths or inspect requests.

days.recap: Use Azure Firewall Premium for TLS inspection and IDPS, NSGs with ASGs for segmentation, private endpoints with private DNS for private and on-premises access, DDoS Network Protection for many IPs and rapid response, Front Door Premium for managed WAF rules and private origins, and pick Front Door, Traffic Manager, Load Balancer or Application Gateway by scope and protocol.

days.title: Final Review: Exam Format, Commonly Confused Pairs, and Test-Day Plan

concepts.heading: Know the Exam Format
concepts.body: AZ-305 is an expert-level, role-based exam, and you pass with a scaled score of 700 or greater. Earning Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect Expert also requires the Azure Administrator Associate certification. The exam page does not state the length or the number of questions; Learn's exam duration page gives 100 minutes for role-based exams without labs (120 minutes of seat time) and 120 minutes for exams that may contain labs, and you are told the exam time when you register. The domains are identity, governance and monitoring 25 to 30 percent, data storage 20 to 25 percent, business continuity 15 to 20 percent, and infrastructure 30 to 35 percent. Expect case studies: a long scenario with tabs for the current environment, requirements and constraints, followed by several questions. Five minutes of break time are built in, but after a break you cannot return to any question you have already seen, including in a case study. Try the exam sandbox to see the item types.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Identity, Governance, and Data Storage
concepts.body: Identity: password hash synchronization lets cloud sign-in keep working when on-premises servers are down, while pass-through authentication validates passwords against on-premises Active Directory; PHS can be kept as a manual backup for PTA. Conditional Access decides when MFA or a compliant device is required; Privileged Identity Management makes privileged roles just-in-time and time-bound. Microsoft Entra roles manage the directory, while Azure RBAC manages Azure resources. Managed identities remove secrets from Azure-hosted code; Key Vault stores the secrets, keys and certificates that remain, and Managed HSM is the single-tenant HSM option. Governance: Azure Policy decides what may exist, RBAC decides who may act, and locks block deletion or change even for owners. Management groups pass policy and access down to subscriptions; tags only label resources and are not inherited unless a policy copies them. Data: SQL Database suits new cloud apps, Managed Instance suits lift-and-shift with SQL Agent and cross-database queries, and SQL Server on VMs gives full OS control. Serverless fits one intermittent database, an elastic pool many. TDE protects data at rest; Always Encrypted hides it from DBAs. Blob access tiers change the cost of storing and reading; redundancy changes which failures data survives. Review days 1 to 11 for any pair that still feels shaky.

concepts.heading: Confused Pairs: Continuity and Infrastructure
concepts.body: Azure Backup keeps recovery points for restore, with an RPO of hours; Site Recovery replicates for failover, with an RPO of minutes. Geo-restore rebuilds a database from backups; active geo-replication keeps readable secondaries per database; a failover group moves several databases together behind unchanged listeners. Availability sets protect against rack failures, zones against datacenter loss, and a second region against regional loss; region pairs never fail over by themselves. ZRS survives a zone, GZRS adds a region, and RA- makes the secondary readable. Service Bus carries business messages, Event Grid pushes discrete events, and Event Hubs ingests streams. App Configuration holds settings and flags; Key Vault holds secrets. Service endpoints keep the public endpoint; private endpoints give a private IP reachable from on-premises. Global Reach links sites, FastPath bypasses the gateway, and Premium reaches other geopolitical regions. Front Door and Application Gateway are Layer 7, Load Balancer is Layer 4, and Traffic Manager is DNS.

concepts.heading: Use an Error Log
concepts.body: In the last days, more questions help less than understanding the ones you missed. Keep an error log with three columns: the topic, the rule you did not know, and the clue in the stem you should have noticed. For example: topic SQL failover, rule the Microsoft managed policy's grace period cannot be under one hour, clue "RTO of 30 minutes". After every practice set, add rows and reread the whole log, and redo missed questions a day later without looking at the answer. Group the rows by domain to see which day of this plan to revisit; infrastructure carries the largest weight, so a weak D4 deserves extra time. Use the question bank's domain filter and the mock exam's one-section option to drill a weak domain, and practise reading case studies by writing down each requirement and constraint before looking at the questions. Stop adding new material the evening before the exam.

concepts.heading: Test-Day Plan
concepts.body: The day before, run a short timed mock, reread your error log and sleep. On the day, check your ID and your testing setup early; for an online proctored exam, clear the desk and test the system ahead of time. In a case study, read the requirements and constraints first, then answer each question against them; a requirement such as minimize cost, no data loss, minimal administrative effort or keep the same connection string usually decides between two plausible designs. Eliminate answers that use retired or retiring features, such as Basic public IPs, Basic Load Balancer or Azure Blueprints. Answer every item, mark long ones for review, and finish your marked items before taking a break, because you cannot return after it. If you do not pass, review the score report by domain. Microsoft's retake policy: wait 24 hours after a first failure, then 14 days between later attempts, with at most five attempts in 12 months from the first.

examPoints: A question that lists Backup, Site Recovery, geo-restore and failover groups together is testing whether you match each technique to the RPO and RTO in the stem rather than to the most powerful option.
A case study question with two plausible designs is testing whether you applied the stated constraint, such as cost, no data loss, data residency or minimal administration, before choosing.

quiz.q: A design review lists two requirements: a stateless web tier must keep serving through a zone outage, and VM recovery points must stay undeletable before expiry even by a vault administrator. Which pair of choices meets both?
choices: An availability set for the web VMs, and soft delete extended to 180 days on the vault
Site Recovery zone-to-zone replication for the web VMs, and Cross Region Restore on a GRS vault
A Uniform scale set in one zone, and multiuser authorization with a Resource Guard on the vault
A Flexible scale set spread across zones, and immutability enabled and locked on the vault
quiz.explain: Spreading the scale set across zones keeps the tier serving through a zone loss, and a locked immutable vault blocks early deletion of recovery points by anyone. Choice A is tempting because both are real protections, but an availability set stays in one datacenter and soft delete still allows deletion.

quiz.q: Which pairing of requirement and service is correct for an expert-level design?
choices: Office-to-office traffic between two ExpressRoute sites calls for FastPath on each virtual network gateway
A non-HTTP game service needing one static anycast IP across regions calls for a global Load Balancer
Reading blob data from another region during an outage without failover calls for GZRS storage
Ordered processing of each customer's commands calls for Event Grid with filtered subscriptions
quiz.explain: The global tier of Azure Load Balancer provides a static anycast IP in front of regional load balancers for any TCP or UDP traffic. Choice A is tempting because FastPath is an ExpressRoute feature, but linking on-premises sites through their circuits is Global Reach.

days.recap: AZ-305 is an expert exam with a scaled pass mark of 700 and a length not stated on the exam page (100 minutes per Learn's duration page for exams without labs); read case studies for their constraints, drill the confused pairs, avoid retired features, answer every item before a break, and know the 24-hour and 14-day retake waits.
